conventions.convention: The lossless plane-wave branch uses a fixed material-rest frame, right-handed Cartesian coordinates, real nonzero k, ω>0, and the phase exp(i(k·x−ωt)). Absolute permittivity is constant, real symmetric positive definite; absolute permeability is a positive real scalar; conductivity is zero.

Complex dot and cross products in the Maxwell symbol and Lorentz reciprocity identity are bilinear without conjugation. Reciprocal coefficients satisfy ordinary transpose symmetry, not Hermitian symmetry.

The reciprocal phasor model permits continuous, spatially varying complex tensor coefficients on a bounded open region with C1 boundary. E and H are C1 on the closure, meaning restrictions of C1 maps on an open neighborhood; J is continuous. The temporal convention is exp(−iωt). No passivity, existence, uniqueness or causal-response assertion is included.

The reciprocity integral uses the outward unit normal, Euclidean volume and boundary area measures, and explicitly assumes Countable Choice. Its boundary integrand is n·(E1×H2−E2×H1), and its volume integrand is E2·J1−E1·J2.

The general uniaxial classification is restricted to k=(kx,0,kz). Only the isotropic specialization explicitly covers arbitrary real wavevector directions. Polarization spaces are complex vector spaces; coincident sheets and optic-axis intersections have dimension two.

The oscillator example assumes a>0, γ>0 and ω>0. Its cycle average uses componentwise complex conjugation and |e|²=Σ|er|², distinct from the unconjugated reciprocity pairing. It concerns a harmonic particular response and qualified model work, without asserting a time-reversal theorem or empirical realization.

load_bearing.statement: For the declared homogeneous source-free lossless branch, M(k,ω)e := k×(μ⁻¹(k×e))+ω²εe. A nonzero amplitude e is a source-free plane-wave mode exactly when M(k,ω)e=0; b=(k×e)/ω, h=b/μ, and k·d=0 for d=εe, while k·e need not vanish.

The fixed-frequency equations are D_j=εE_j, B_j=μH_j, curl E_j=iωB_j, and curl H_j=J_j−iωD_j. The coefficient model is reciprocal when ε(x)^T=ε(x) and μ(x)^T=μ(x) pointwise; neither product conjugates either input.

Assume Countable Choice. For two C1 phasor solutions on a bounded C1 domain, with continuous sources and common continuous transpose-symmetric complex constitutive tensors, ∫∂Ω n·(E1×H2−E2×H1) dS = ∫Ω (E2·J1−E1·J2) dV. Products are complex-bilinear, and both integrals have units W. The lossless anisotropic plane-wave branch is a subcase.

For positive principal permittivities, positive scalar permeability, ω>0 and real k=(kx,0,kz)≠0, nonzero-mode wavevectors lie on kx²+kz²=με⊥ω² or kx²/ε∥+kz²/ε⊥=μω². Away from intersections the ordinary y sector and extraordinary xz sector each have one-dimensional polarization space; at intersections their span has dimension two. Unequal principal permittivities intersect only on the optic axis. In the isotropic specialization arbitrary real directions are allowed, with |k|²=μεω² and polarization space {e∈C³:k·e=0}.
